newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on market liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on market liquidity.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates extended earlier falls to close down 130 basis points at 23.50 percent on Monday in a market awash with liquidity from foreign capital inflow, traders said.
"Although rates fell in part after recent unrepresentative high closing rates, foreigners are still stepping in, which we can see from the peso's firmness," one trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.6 of a centavo firmer at 7.8240/7.8280 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 95 basis points at 24.80 percent.
Other traders said rates returned to a downward trend due to changes in forecasts for the central bank's primary auction on Tuesday.

"As recently as Friday, we were expecting rates to adjust upwards. Demand for term instruments has picked up, however," said one trader, who expected bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to fall 25-50 basis points.
Banco de Mexico assigned 28-day Cetes at 24.24 percent last week.
Dealers said forecasts of a downward trend in domestic inflation during the first half of 1997 triggered demand for term paper among local and foreign investors.
Banco de Mexico drained a liquidity surplus arising from money returning to the system through two auctions to drain 806 million pesos, which it assigned at rates of 24.91 percent and 25.39 percent.
Liquidity of 300 million pesos is expected to return to the system on Tuesday.
